facts.fact: UNESCO reports that regulators and policymakers from Guinea-Bissau, with Angola, Sao Tome and Principe and Mozambique (more than 40 in all), took part in a data governance workshop in Maputo on 8-10 December 2025, organised by UNESCO with Mozambique's INTIC and Smart Africa; attendance only, no agreement signed.

facts.fact: AUDA-NEPAD, the African Union's development agency, launched on 24 July 2026 at the STC-TTIM ministerial segment in Abidjan its Programme for African Developing Island Economies, which Guinea-Bissau joins with six other island states; digital transformation is one of its six pillars, and the programme runs on a 2026-2031 roadmap.

facts.fact: ECOWAS says Guinea-Bissau is one of the implementers of the first series of the World Bank-funded WARDIP, running 2024 to 2028 with the ECOWAS Commission, the African Union and Smart Africa.
ECOWAS says the WARDIP Regional Project Coordination Committee held its inaugural meeting on 11 November 2025, with Guinea-Bissau among the implementing countries.
ECOWAS says Guinea-Bissau is a key implementing partner of the DTfA/WARDIP regional digital integration programme, alongside ECOWAS, Smart Africa and the African Union Commission.
